item.title: TONIGHT | Keller & The Keels w/sg Tanasi — Sat Aug 29 — French Broad River Brewery
item.description:
Saturday, August 29 • 7 PM – 11 PM | From $45.70 Event Details and Tickets Musical Mad Scientist Keller Williams brings his Appalachian Psychedelic Bluegrass project, Keller & the Keels, to the stage on Saturday, August 29 with special guest Tanasi. Joining him are award-winning flatpicker Larry Keel and his rock-solid, in-the-pocket bass-playing wife, Jenny Keel. The trio—formed in 2004—has recorded three albums together (Grass, Thief, and Speed), and with only a handful of shows each year, every performance turns into a joyful, high-energy acoustic picking party. As Keller puts it, “We vowed from the beginning that we wouldn’t do it often so that when we did, it would be special—and it is.” 2026 marks the 20th anniversary of Grass, Keller & the Keels’ first album together. After two decades, Grass finally gets its first-ever vinyl pressing—available on site and ready to roll.

item.title: The Legacy Neighborhood Coalition Festival — Sat Aug 29, 12:00 PM — Memorial Stadium (Asheville)
item.description: The Legacy Neighborhood Coalition Festival is a free, family-friendly celebration honoring the people, history, and traditions of Asheville’s legacy neighborhoods. Held at Memorial Stadium on August 28–29, 2026, the festival brings together the communities of Burton Street, East End/Valley Street, Emma, Shiloh, and Southside for a weekend filled with music, food, storytelling, art, youth activities, and cultural experiences. Designed as a community homecoming, the Legacy Neighborhood Coalition Festival invites residents, former neighbors, legacy families, and visitors to reconnect through shared stories, neighborhood pride, and collective celebration. Festival highlights include live performances, local vendors, family activities, cultural demonstrations, community exhibits, and a special neighborhood tour experience that connects visitors to the rich history of Asheville’s legacy communities. Join us as we celebrate the people, places, and traditions that continue to shape Asheville.

item.title: Asheville Symphony Presents - Masterworks 1: Fellowship — Sat Aug 29, 2:00 PM — First Baptist Church of Asheville
item.description:
Two performances, 2 p.m. and 8 p.m. Event Details and Tickets
SATURDAY, SEPTEMBER 26, 2026 2:00 P.M. AND 8:00 P.M. FIRST BAPTIST CHURCH OF ASHEVILLE Darko Butorac, conductor Jakob Aumiller, piano
What does genius look like? Often it looks like community. Brahms crafted his exuberant First Piano Concerto through years of collaboration with close friends and mentors, including Clara Schumann who inspired the concerto’s dreamy second movement. Beethoven’s relentless Seventh Symphony — a personal favorite of his with its unyielding rhythmic drive — premiered at a charity concert performed by an orchestra of friends and fellow composers. Both works emerged from profound creative kinship and community, proof that greatness rarely stands alone. Brahms: Piano Concerto No. 1 Beethoven: Symphony No. 7

item.description: Hendo Fun Friends I am going to unravel my stress at Otter Hole Swimmin’ Hole at the headwaters of the So.Mills River. item.title: Geology of the Blue Ridge Field Class — Thu Sep 17, 11:00 AM
item.description:
Geology of the Blue Ridge Field Class with Anton DuMars Thursday, September 17 | 11am – 5pm BRN – Core Register Here!
On this Field Experience, we will observe and interpret evidence of Appalachian mountain-building events. Participants can put their hands on a 380+/- million-year-old pluton and observe their post-uplift weathering, jointing, and exfoliation. In addition, participants observe and interpret river processes, transport, and depositional environments of sediments derived from up-gradient sources. The experience includes on-site geologic map reading and interpretation. This off-site program has stops in the Pisgah Forest near Brevard NC along The Pisgah Highway including Daniel Ridge and the Davidson River. This program provides transportation to and from the class location using our minibus. We will meet at the Arboretum and return to the Arboretum. item.title: Tour des Trees — Thu Sep 17, 2:00 PM
item.description: Tour des Trees September 17, 2026 from 2 pm to 4:30 pm On September 17th The NC Arboretum will be hosting the Tour des Trees cyclists and organizers for an afternoon of presentations open to the public. The Tour des Trees is an annual long-distance cycling adventure which serves as the primary public outreach and community engagement event for Tree Research and Education Endowment Fund (TREE Fund). Since 1992, Tour des Trees riders have cycled through communities in the U.S., Canada, and the U.K., planting trees, educating children and shining a light on the work done by arboriculture professionals and the importance of science-based tree care. The 2026 Tour des Trees will take place from Saturday, September 12 to Friday, September 18. The programs here at the Arboretum will start at 2 pm with an Ask the Arborist presentation and a special kids program will start at 3:45 pm with Professor Pricklethorn. item.title: Buncombe County Parks Update - Open and Closed Parks — Thu Nov 5
item.description: Email: parks@buncombecounty.orgPhone: (828) 250-4260Notice - Description: Information about Open and Closed ParksMany Buncombe County Parks were impacted by Hurricane Helene. While we are working diligently reopen parks as quickly as we can, some parks continue to remain closed. Please see the list below for which parks are open and which parks continue to be closed for safety reasons.OPEN Parks: Lake Julian Park (please note, some disc golf holes remain closed), Hominy Valley Park, Collier Cove Nature Preserve, North Buncombe Fields, Cane Creek Playground, Buncombe County Sports Park, Corcoran Paige River Park, Bent Creek River Park, Ledges Whitewater Park, and Hominy Creek River Park. If people choose to recreate on the river, we strongly encourage them to be aware of changes on streambanks and in the riverbed and the potential for unknown debris from Helene.CLOSED Parks: Charles D.
